messages:
From: Sarah White <sarah.white@novapay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10 21:02:00 -0700
Subject: DPA request and subprocessor mapping for NovaPay onboarding

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo today — NovaPay’s legal and security teams would like to get a DPA in place before we move to PO. Can you share Redwood’s current DPA template and your current subprocessor mapping?

A few specific asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood executes SCCs (EU->US) or uses another mechanism.
- We need a brief technical dataflow diagram or the endpoints that will receive PII so our network team can allowlist.
- Please provide SOC 2 Type II evidence (or summary) and your most recent security attestation.
- Preferred execution method: AdobeSign or DocuSign? We prefer AdobeSign but can adapt.
- Timeline: legal would like a signed DPA within two weeks if possible.

Thanks,
Sarah White
Head of Legal Operations, NovaPay
procurement@novapay.com

Subject: Re: DPA request and subprocessor mapping for NovaPay onboarding

Sarah — great to meet you earlier. Attaching our standard DPA template (Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2_redline.docx) and the current subprocessor manifest (subprocessor_manifest.csv).

Quick notes:
- We execute SCCs as the default transfer mechanism for EU personal data; the DPA includes the SCC Annex. If you have a different transfer mechanism preference, flag it and our legal team will review.
- Default e-sign: DocuSign. We can use AdobeSign if you prefer — we just need to know before we send the envelope.
- SOC 2 Type II: see attached Redwood_Security_Attestation_2026Q2.pdf and the short SOC summary in the DPA footnote.
- Technical dataflow: here’s a read-only diagram link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d5E/redwood-novapay-dataflow-diagram (contains endpoint IPs and brief flow notes).

Marissa — looping you in for any redline guidance. Karthik, can you pick up procurement follow-up for PO and invoicing?

I’ll stand by for any questions; happy to hop on a quick call with your security team next week if helpful.

—Sean
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA request and subprocessor mapping for NovaPay onboarding

Hi Sarah — thanks, Sean. A few clarifications from legal after a quick review of the template:

1) Retention / deletion: our standard clause requires data deletion or return within 60 days of termination unless otherwise agreed. If NovaPay requires a longer retention period for litigation hold, please propose the language.

2) Subprocessor notice: Redwood provides advance notice of material additions to subprocessors and publishes a manifest. We typically provide 30 days’ notice before onboarding a new subprocessor; we can discuss expedited notice for specific vendors on your allowlist.

3) Audit rights: we can accommodate annual audits or reviews via a third-party attestation (SOC 2) in lieu of direct on-site audits. If NovaPay requires on-site audits, we’ll need to route to our GVP approval — please confirm your preference.

4) Cross-border transfers: DPA includes SCC Annex for EU transfers. For requests to replace SCCs with an alternative mechanism, please list the specific legal basis.

5) De-identified / aggregated telemetry: we reserve the right to collect aggregated usage metrics but will not include NovaPay-identifiable content in telemetry exports.

Attaching the Redwood Security Attestation (Redwood_Security_Attestation_2026Q2.pdf) to expedite your review. If there are any material legal redlines, please surface them and indicate which are must-haves vs. negotiable.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah White <sarah.white@novapay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@novapay.com>
Date: 2026-09-11 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA request and subprocessor mapping for NovaPay onboarding

Marissa / Sean — thanks for the quick responses and attachments. A few follow-ups from our security and procurement teams:

- AdobeSign vs DocuSign: procurement prefers AdobeSign. If you can only send DocuSign, we can accept; preference is not a blocker.
- Subprocessor cadence: 30 days’ notice is reasonable. Can you confirm how frequently the manifest is published (monthly / quarterly)?
- Allowlisting: can you provide a short list of IP ranges and FQDNs that our network team can allowlist? The dataflow link was helpful but our ops team wants explicit ranges.
- Audit rights: we prefer annual review; SOC 2 + Redwood Security Attestation works for now. If an on-site audit is ever requested, we will flag it early.
- On-prem option: NovaPay is considering an on-premise connector for high-sensitivity flows. Is there a supported path or appliance for air-gapped transfer for just a small subset of data?

Attaching NovaPay’s preliminary risk assessment (nova_risk_assessment.xlsx) for context.

If everything looks good we’ll aim to review redlines this week and get procurement to issue the PO next week.

Thanks,
Sarah White
Head of Legal Operations, NovaPay

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sarah White <sarah.white@novapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@novapay.com>
Date: 2026-09-12 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA request and subprocessor mapping for NovaPay onboarding

Sarah — thanks for the detailed notes. Answers inline: 

- E-sign: we will send a DocuSign envelope today by default. If NovaPay would like AdobeSign instead, we can switch but need a contact for the AdobeSign admin to accept the invite.
- Manifest cadence: the subprocessor manifest is updated quarterly and published to the same shared folder; for material changes we provide 30 days’ notice.
- Allowlist: I’ve pasted a short allowlist summary in the shared diagram file and will export IP ranges as a CSV. If you need CIDR ranges only, we can provide that to your network team by EOD.
- On-prem connector: we do offer a private deployment option (Redwood Private) for regulated workloads; I’ll have solutions engineering follow up with a short runbook and high-level cost estimate if you’re interested in a PoC.
- Audit: annual third-party attestation plus ad-hoc reviews by exception is our standard; we’ll note NovaPay’s preference for annual reviews in the DPA.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) We will send the DocuSign envelope with the DPA template (redlines included) today.
2) I’ll upload the IP ranges CSV to the shared Drive and send a direct link.
3) Karthik will follow up on procurement / PO and send invoicing details.

Attachments included in this thread: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2_redline.docx, subprocessor_manifest.csv, Redwood_Security_Attestation_2026Q2.pdf, nova_risk_assessment.xlsx

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9876543/DP-2026-0912-NOVA
Dataflow & allowlist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d5E/redwood-novapay-dataflow-diagram

If that timeline works I’ll mark the task complete and watch for the signed envelope. Happy to jump on a follow-up call to walk procurement/security through details — Karthik, can you propose times?

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
